_comment:
CAPABILITY suite for the Db2 CDC stream source, via `--type connectors/db2cdc.json`. Functions in functions/caps_db2cdc.py. Four @stream_publisher variants over the ASN SQL-Replication CD tables of the seeded db2cdc_employees_xs domain, each tracking the employees model's two MUTABLE tables (employees: insert/update/delete, departments: update) -> 2 slots, 2 output tables (emp_changes / dept_changes) per collection: base (tail = each CD table's current watermark, flattened tabular rows), _head (start_from=head, replays each CD table from the origin; registration precedes create-data, so the seed load arrives as inserts), _struct (columns_format=struct, flatten_columns=False; registrations use `image both`, so old values are present), _map (columns_format=map, new values still inlined). ONE COLLECTION PER VARIANT (one connection each, all from the same template — Db2 needs no per-stream id: each consumer just reads the CD table and tracks its own offset, so the four coexist). NOTE `tables` names the CD tables (ASN.TD_T__EMPLOYEES / ASN.TD_T__DEPARTMENTS, uppercase as Db2 folds them), not the source tables — the ingester resolves the source via ASN.IBMSNAP_REGISTER; the ASN schema is shared while the source schema is per-domain, so ONE db2cdc domain per model at a time (the staging name has no domain qualifier). NO TRIGGERS, and none are needed: REGISTERING a stream publisher STARTS it — the worker comes up seconds after `create-project` and runs until you `tdk fn disable`/`fn delete` it (a stream worker has no execution plan or transaction; find it with `tdk worker list`). To exercise: (1) `tdx-xp oneshot --suite connectors/db2cdc --keep` (or create-project), (2) generate changes with `tdx-domain modify-data --domain _db2cdc_employees_xs --ops Mix --sets 5` (Insert|Update|Delete|Mix), (3) watch batches land with `tdk trx list --proj

--monitor` and the workers with `tdk worker list`. `oneshot` WITHOUT --keep tears the project down again, which also stops the streams. Capture is asynchronous (asncap stages into the CD table first), so a change takes a moment longer to appear than on MySQL/Postgres.
